newsitem.title: UK: NWE gasoline rallies on French buying, arbitrage.
newsitem.headline: NWE gasoline rallies on French buying, arbitrage.

text.p: NWE gasoline rallied sharply on Monday on French buying that some traders speculated was tied to the strike at three Elf Aquitaine refineries which entered its fifth day.
"It's in small quantities but it's a positive feature," said a London broker. "Plus NYMEX (gasoline) is up and crude is up."
Sharply higher NYMEX gasoline futures that appeared to keep the arbitrage to the U.S. open also boosted NWE barges and cargoes, traders said.
French buying entered the market today for a parcel of leaded and one of Superplus, traders said.
Some speculated the amounts were for 8,000 to 10,000 tonnes and were sold on a quotes related basis, but this was not confirmed.
One London trader said France is predominantly a user of the higher run material, which would be more available in the north than in the Med.
Oil workers on Monday voted to extend the strike into Tuesday and raised the stakes by demanding the same early retirement right just won by victorious French truckers.
The stricken Elf plants make up a quarter of French capacity and three quarters of Elf's European refining network.
Elf officials said there was no shortage of fuel since depots were mostly full after the trucker's blockade.
Eurograde barges ended up $7 at $214/$216 fob ARA with afternoon deals at $214.25 and $213 for a 2,000 tonne barge fob Amsterdam-Rotterdam for loading Dec 4-15.
Regular unleaded ended up $5 at $205/$207 fob ARA and Superplus up $3 at $235/$237.
Premium unleaded cargoes notionally were assessed at $228/$230 cif, up $2 from Friday.
